questions.question: A manufacturer claims that the variance in the diameter of rods produced is 4 mm². A sample of 10 rods gives a sample variance of 6 mm². Test at the 5% level of significance whether the population variance differs from 4 mm². / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Null hypothesis Ho : б2 = 4 - 1 mark,
  • Alternate hypothesis H1 : б2 ≠ 4 - 1 mark,
  • Test statistic χ2 =
  • (𝑛−1)𝑠2
  • 𝜎02 = 13.5 – 2 marks
  • Conclusion – 2 mark
  • (At 5% level of significance, we fail to reject the null hypothesis, as the
  • calculated chi-square value of 13.5 does not exceed the critical threshold.)

questions.question: On the basis of their total scores, 200 candidates of a civil service examination are divided into two groups: the upper 30 percent and the remaining 70 percent. Consider the first question in the examination. Among the first group, 40 had the correct answer, whereas among the second group, 80 had the correct answer. On the basis of these results, can one conclude that the first question is not good at discriminating the ability of the candidates examined? / [CO3] [12x1 = 12]
questions.solution_html:
• Null hypothesis Ho : p1 = p2 - 1 mark,
  • Alternate hypothesis H1 : p1 > p2 - 1 mark,
  • p1= 0.667-1 mark,p2 = 0.571 -1 mark,
  • Test statistic equation – 2 marks
  • Test statistic t =1.23 – 2 marks
  • Table value 𝑡∝/2 = 1.96 - 1 mark
  • Conclusion – 2 mark, no reason to reject H0
